column1: Shared memory (one memory connecting the four intelligences)
column2: Contextual learning and auditability claims, not an explicit shared-organizational-memory promise: page title 'AI agents that learn from your best sales conversations'; 'Every team has plays of its own... Attention builds the agent'; 'All actions auditable and traceable'; insights written to systems of record; MCP access to Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor over 70+ read/write tools (https://www.attention.com/)
column3: Activity-capture memory framing, not explicit shared-memory language: 'We give revenue teams the backstory on every deal, account and customer interaction'; 'Backstory reads every call, email, and CRM record across the quarter'; 'analyzes two years of your deal history on day one' (https://www.backstory.ai/)
column4: 'Knowledge' innovation card: 'Upload proprietary sales and positioning content such as case studies, white papers, and competitive battlecards directly into the Outreach AI knowledge base to inform AI personalization agent and smart assist.'; MCP: 'Let information and actions flow freely across your GTM stack' (https://www.outreach.ai/)
column5: Promise: 'Know every deal. Coach every rep. Forget nothing.'; one memory in three layers. Layer 1 ('What was said') is backed by Built call capture (calendar sync, transcripts, call summaries) and documents (Content Library); its email and Slack sources are In build / Planned. In build: 'Memory layers two and three: what calls meant, and what happened next'. Flagged by the Narrative: 'Connecting the dots (the pricing example)'.
column6: Overlap: all three ground AI output in accumulated deal/account knowledge on the inspected pages. Difference: Backstory's brand IS memory ('backstory on every deal', two years of history analyzed on day one); Attention frames memory as agent learning plus auditability; Outreach abstracts it into the Knowledge card and MCP stack flow. None uses the phrase 'shared memory' or claims one memory connecting multiple intelligence types. Provisional implication: PitchSense's integrated-memory framing is not verbatim-claimed by any of these three, but differentiation depends on how visibly the connection is demonstrated — test whether the integration itself (call→deal→content→coaching) is the promise, not just 'memory'. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): PitchSense's own layers 2–3 and its deal links are In build, so the 'call→deal→content→coaching' integration cannot be demonstrated publicly yet; today only calls→summaries and documents→practice are Built.

column5: Built: transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Fireflies, Fathom and Granola; summaries and pre-call brief delivered to Slack; documents via the Content Library. In build: reading email for deal context (Gmail, Outlook); summaries by email and Teams; meeting bot. Planned: CRM connection (Salesforce, HubSpot) and updates; reading deal conversations in Slack; deal status from email and Slack. Flagged: 'The CRM use cases'; 'Everything about email and Slack tracking'.
column6: Overlap: all three claim multi-channel capture (Attention: 200+ integrations and recorder ingest; Backstory: Salesforce/Dynamics/Oracle/Gmail/Outlook/Zoom/Teams/Slack; Outreach: Omni across accounts/opportunities/prospects/meetings in-app/mobile/Slack). Difference: Backstory emphasizes automatic matching to accounts/opportunities; Attention emphasizes agent access; Outreach emphasizes conversational action. Provisional implication: channel lists are table stakes; the differentiator to test is what the connected channels produce (answers vs data), which is where Backstory already plays. NARRATIVE V1 RECONCILIATION (Oct 19, 2026): PitchSense can claim calls (transcripts) and documents today; CRM, email and Slack are In build or Planned, so the channel list is not a public claim yet.
